texas.label: Texas
texas._validate: open-trench limit for a Texas city; examples elsewhere are 300 ft (Sacramento County, end of day) and 200 ft (Framingham)
texas.signature: Soft saturated clay over a shallow water table. No rock at all.
texas._hazard_source: Hazard Matrix sheet; V.High = severe hazard (soil cohesion V.High means dangerously weak ground; bedrock depth Low means rock too deep to matter)
texas._situations_validate: no E2: bedrock depth Low means no rock

money._source: LOB-Game Sandbox: deadline = default plan finish + 12 days; budget = finish x daily fleet cost x 1.3 + $60,000

workbookDurations._source: LOB Disruption Event Library Final7, Response Option sheet (Base Rate Drop, Duration). rateDrop is the fraction LOST: the crew works at (1 - rateDrop). Where the Situations sheet disagrees (E1 1 day, P3 1-2 days, B1 2 days) the game uses the Response Option sheet's value.

E1.name: Buried utility or existing pipeline strike

E2.name: Unforeseen ground conditions, hard rock refusal

P1.name: Trench collapse / cave-in
P1._validate: the sheet's Day column reads 2/1/0 for option A (own machine) and 3/2/1 for option C (hired); the game uses 3/2/1 clearing days for both, lender loses the same days

P2.name: Late pipe delivery / supply chain lag

P3.name: Pipe dropped during lifting / rigging failure

B1.name: Poor backfill compaction density / QC test failure
